item.title: A machine-checked proof of the Dong-Yang classification of optimal (n,4) binary codes for BSCs
item.description: arXiv:2609.10579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a machine-checked Lean~4 formalization of Dong and Yang's classification of optimal finite-length $(n,4)$ binary block codes for binary symmetric channels. The formalization was developed mainly by feeding the paper's proofs to an AI tool. To establish correctness, the authors verified the main theorem statements in Lean and the accepted axioms. This note discusses the corrections and simplifications made to the AI-generated formalization, and records discrepancies found in the paper during the formalization. The Lean code is available at https://github.com/shhyang/n4code_lean.
item.dc:creator: Shenghao Yang, Yanyan Dong

item.title: A General Approach to Enharmonicism
item.description: arXiv:2609.10603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a general approach to enharmonicism within syntactic music theory; that is, we formalize several abstract structures of enharmonicism without any acoustic considerations. The structures of concern to this paper are constructed from diatonics, chromatics, and enharmonics, and we seek to present a general enharmonic theory that builds upon Hook's enharmonic theory published in "Enharmonic Systems: A Theory of Key Signatures, Enharmonic Equivalence and Diatonicism" (2007). We also propose that the two criteria of reflection and maximal evenness can be used to determine whether an arbitrary enharmonic system is musically practical. Moreover, we argue that preferential treatment of the standard enharmonic system (SES) can be motivated from an abstract mathematical perspective divorced from pitch consideration and conventional acoustic constructions of SES.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Scott Alons

item.title: Some Early Results by Tutte Regarding the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture in 1948
item.description: arXiv:2609.10618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OpenAI recently announced a proof of the Cycle Double Cover (CDC) Conjecture. Most media reports have characterized it as a 50-year-old open problem. In reality, according to a 1987 letter from Tutte to Fleischner, the Cycle Double Cover Problem has been open for at least 80 years. Two early results regarding the CDC conjecture were established in one of Tutte's 1949 publications.
item.dc:creator: Cun-Quan Zhang

item.title: Perspectives on the unit distance problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.10791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a survey on an old open problem in combinatorics called the unit distance problem, and the field of mathematics around it, called incidence geometry. What do we know about the problem? Why is it difficult? How does it connect with other parts of math?
item.dc:creator: Larry Guth
